subject: Private GPU pool stress plan & network guardrails

Subject: Kickoff: Private GPU pool for Acme - capacity & networking questions

Hi Soojin / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. We're kicking off procurement for a private VPC deployment of Redwood's inference runtime for a high-throughput customer-facing feature. Before we finalize contracts we need a concrete capacity and networking plan that covers:

- Sustained throughput target: ~200 inference requests/sec (model avg response ~300 tokens).
- Burst scenarios: up to ~600 req/sec for short spikes (10-20m) during product launches.
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 300ms for typical 512-token responses.
- Network constraints: we plan to run in a single AZ with limited cross-AZ egress; typical backend fabric is 100Gbps with 2 x 25Gb NICs on servers.

Concrete asks: can Redwood provide a recommended GPU pool sizing, autoscaling policy (rules for warm vs. cold scale), and network guardrails (NAT, egress, MTU, jumbo frames) plus a short stress test plan? We also need to understand fallback behavior to hosted Redwood API if private pool saturates.

I've attached a small sample traffic trace and current infra snapshot. Let us know what additional telemetry you need.

Attachments: [acme-capacity-snapshot.csv (CSV, 38KB)]

Thanks,
Acme Infra Team
infra@acme.com

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Private GPU pool for Acme - capacity & networking questions

Hi — thanks for the trace and clear asks. High level answers up front and then a list of follow-ups:

1) Baseline recommendation (prelim): size to handle sustained 200 req/s with 40% headroom => target pool able to absorb ~280 req/s sustained, with autoscale policy for bursts to 600 req/s for 15 minutes.
2) Architecture: dedicated VPC-resident pool with a warm standby capacity (hot cache nodes + preloaded KV caches); optional short-circuit fallback to Redwood-hosted instances if private capacity is exhausted (requires routing policy & auth config).
3) Network guardrails: recommend colocated model storage on NVMe; MTU 9000 enabled across fabric; ensure NAT throughput > 10Gbps per gateway; enable flow logs for egress monitoring.

Follow-ups (please provide these so we can finalize numbers):
- Typical request token distribution (median / 90 / 95 token counts) and percent of requests that use tool calling or function outputs.
- Expected QPS per regional endpoint (even if single AZ today).
- Confirmation on tolerated failover window and whether fallback to hosted Redwood is acceptable for 1-2% error budget.

I'm attaching a quick workbook with preliminary sizing math and a network checklist to validate with your infra team.

Attachments: [prelim-sizing-math.xlsx (XLSX, 56KB), network-checklist.md (MD, 7KB)]

Proposed next steps: 30m call tomorrow to walk the math, and a stress-run plan doc after we align on token distribution.

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Private GPU pool for Acme - capacity & networking questions

Adding sizing detail from infra planning team side — ran quick sims against the trace Soojin received. Highlights and assumptions below:

Assumptions:
- Model: 11B dense (~512 token typical inference), using q4_k_m quant profile or fp16 on A100 for latency profile.
- Per-GPU concurrency: 7-10 concurrent streams for A100-80GB with optimized kernel stack; roughly 60-80 tokens/sec per GPU under our runtime when batching is enabled.

Prelim numbers:
- For sustained 280 req/s effective (including 40% headroom) we estimate 6 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (with pinning across nodes) as the baseline.
- For burst-to-600 req/s for 15m we recommend either 3 prewarmed smaller instances (e.g., T4/RTX as burst nodes) or a scheduled short-term scale-up to 10 GPUs total (autoscale threshold + warm-up window).
- Headroom: reserve 30-40% buffer for KV-cache warmup and model weight I/O.

Network notes:
- Ensure server NICs are bonded; allow jumbo frames MTU 9000 across switch + host.
- NAT instance sizing needs to support peak egress + health-check traffic; recommend separate egress NAT cluster to avoid throttling inference traffic.

Operational:
- Cache warming: preload common prefixes detected in your trace into the KV cache before launches (we can supply tools to generate warm-up traffic).
- Rollout: start at 60% commit of baseline pool, run 24h soak with production-sim traffic, then scale to baseline + headroom.

I've attached a CSV with the sim estimates and a short PDF with batching sim results. These are conservative — if you can tolerate p95 350ms we can reduce GPU count by ~1-2 and rely more on quantization.

Attachments: [sizing-estimates.csv (CSV, 48KB), batching-sim-results.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

Couple of engineering caveats / tips from runtime side:

- Quantization: "q4_k_m" gives good latency/cost tradeoff but requires careful kernel selection. If you run mixed precision (fp16) on A100, you can reduce variance at the cost of higher memory usage.
- Batching policy: set target batch window to 8–12ms for product-facing low-latency use; dynamic batching is fine but enforce a max batch size to bound latency.
- KV/Prefix caching: ensure Redis or local PB cache has throughput > 200k ops/s for warm-up traffic and persistence on NVMe for faster reloads.
- Network: enable IRQ affinity and multiqueue on NICs; watch for CPU-side serialization if using small instance types. Jumbo frames (MTU 9000) across the path reduces CPU overhead for large model shards transfer.
- Storage: use local NVMe for model weights and an S3-compatible object store for cold-tier. Ensure model weight load time is < 25s for a cold start to meet burst scaling windows — otherwise consider preloaded standby nodes.

Linking to a running Jira for infra tasks: JIRA: INFRA-1284 (private-pool stress test plan) and a drive folder with stress artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-sim

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps: 

Summary decisions:
- Baseline commit: 6 x A100-80GB equivalent (handles 280 req/s with 40% headroom).
- Burst strategy: autoscale to 10 GPUs for 15 minutes on spike OR warm T4 burst nodes as a cheaper buffer; final choice dependent on Acme cost/latency tradeoff.
- Network guardrails: MTU 9000, bonded NICs, separate NAT egress cluster sized > 10Gbps, enable VPC flow logs.
- Fallback: allow hosted Redwood fallback for up to 2% of requests during exceptional saturation (we will confirm auth/routing).

Action items and owners:
- Acme: share token distribution percentiles and confirm allowed fallback window by Tue 2028-09-19 (Assigned: infra@acme.com).
